W. C. L., Canaanite Myths and Legends, 2nd ed. (Edinburgh 1978); Ginsberg, H. L., 'The Ugaritic Texts and the Old Testament,' in J. B. Pritchard (ed.), Ancient Near Eastern Texts (Princeton 1955; orig. monograph 1936); Saunders, M. (ed.), Digital Semitics Online Library (DSOL), Ugaritic Inscriptions section (https://m-saunders.com/ugaritic-inscriptions/, accessed 2026-06-02) — used for verification of KTU 1.1 ii-v transliteration.
source.fragmentationNote: KTU 1.1 is severely fragmentary: columns i, vi destroyed; column ii partially recovered (~25 lines, mostly heavy lacunae); column iii partially recovered (~30 lines, lacunae throughout); column iv preserves ~32 substantive lines (the most-recovered portion of KTU 1.1, including the famous name-giving scene 'šm bny yw'); column v preserves ~28 fragmentary lines. KTU 1.2 column ii is broken away entirely; columns i, iii, iv preserve the main narrative of Yammu's embassy (i, ~46 lines), pre-duel material (iii, ~25 lines), and the duel itself with Baʿlu's victory (iv, ~40 lines). Lacunae marked per project lacuna-bracket convention: [...] = total lacuna; [text] = restored from parallels; <text> = editorial addition; {text} = editorial deletion.
source.scriptNote: Ugaritic alphabetic cuneiform — 30 letters (Northwest-Semitic abjad rendered in cuneiform wedges) + word divider. Unlike Sumero-Akkadian logographic cuneiform, this is a 1:1 transliteration-to-Unicode mapping. Strict KTU transliteration convention: every alef explicitly marked as ʾa/ʾi/ʾu (the three letter forms in the script). Bare vowels in popular vocalized transliterations (e.g. ʾaliyn) represent comparative-Semitics reconstructions and are NOT separately in the script; strict consonantal-skeletal forms used here (ʾalʾiyn for the same word, since the medial /i/ IS an alef-i letter in the script). Word divider 𐎟 (U+1039F) between words in the cuneiform rendering. Cuneiform output in this file was produced mechanically by the project's translit_to_ugaritic.py helper from each line's transliteration — not hand-authored.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.1 col i: destroyed — no preserved text. The opening of the Cycle is lost; from the surviving narrative arc (Smith 1994 vol 1, pp. 152-156) the lost opening probably set the scene of the divine assembly at the abode of ʾIlu (= El) on Mount Lel and announced Yammu's exaltation as challenger to Baʿlu.]

[KTU 1.1 col ii: top of column lost; preserved text begins mid-speech with what appears to be a divine summons-formula (the 'hasten your feet' speed-of-travel formula characteristic of divine messenger-speeches throughout the Cycle).]

lines.notes: The standard 'hasten' (ḥwš) summons-formula opening: '[Hasten, urge, speed to] me your feet…'
'…[let them race to me, let] your legs [hasten].' Smith 1994 vol 1 reads this as the standard parallelism pʿn // ʾišd 'foot' // 'leg' (lower-leg).
'[Into the midst of the mountain G]R(?) [is] your statement, and set…' Reconstructed; the destination-formula varies by addressee (Mount Lel for ʾIlu; Mount Ṣapunu for Baʿlu).
'…upon your shoulder(?).' rdy 'shoulder/back' — body-part vocabulary; sense uncertain.
'…lapis-lazuli.' Material reference; possibly part of an instruction-list for cultic preparation.
'…he lifts in the midst (of).' yšʾu = G-yqtl of nšʾ 'to lift, raise (the voice/hand).'
'…ʾasr.' ʾasr = either G-pf 'I bound' or D-impv 'bind!'; context lost.
'…(those) days, two days.' Day-doubling-formula characteristic of Ugaritic narrative time-passage (cf. ym . ymm 'day, days'; ṯlṯ ym 'three days').
'…[his throa]t and [I will] go(?).' npš (throat/breath/self) here likely literal anatomical.
'…[crafts]men set down to the earth.' ḥršm = 'craftsmen, artisans' (cf. Hebrew ḥārāš); foreshadows the Kothar craftsman-deity material later.
'…lips(?) set down.' špm = 'lips'; reading uncertain.
'…they pass by.' tʿtqn = Gt-yqtl 3mp of ʿtq 'to pass on, advance.'
'…return(?), your god.' šb possibly impv of ṯwb 'return'; ʾilk = 'your god(s).'
'…there is no entryway in the thousand-courts(?).' ʾin = negative existential 'there is not'; bb = doorway; ʾalp ḥẓr = 'thousand court(s),' a numerical pair-formula.
'[At the f]eet of ʿAnatu.' Introducing the bowing-before-Anat scene. ʿAnatu (ʿnt) is the warrior-consort goddess, sister-and-partner of Baʿlu.
'[He bows and falls down, he] prostrates himself and (gives) hon[or to her]...' The standard prostration-formula throughout the Cycle (hbr-yql-yštḥwy-kbd four-verb sequence).
'[Honors her, he raises his voice and] cries — Message of…' The standard message-delivery formula (yšʾu gh wyṣḥ) followed by tḥm 'message of (X) (to Y).'
'[Bull ʾIlu, your father, word of the Be]nevolent-One, your patriarch.' ṯr ʾil 'Bull-El' standard epithet; lṭpn 'Benevolent' standard epithet of ʾIlu; ḥtk 'patriarch, head-of-lineage.'

lines.translit: [qryy . b ʾarṣ . mlḥ]mt . št b ʿp
lines.notes: '[Place in the earth wa]r, set in the du[st…]'. The famous peace-making oracle (parallel KTU 1.3 III; 1.3 IV; 1.7) — cf. Isa 2:4 'beat swords into plowshares.'

lines.translit: [rm . ddym . sk . šlm] . l kbd . ʾarṣ
lines.notes: '[…mandrakes(?), pour peace] into the midst of the earth.' The cosmic-pacification oracle. ddym 'love-tokens / mandrakes / mounds'; kbd ʾarṣ 'midst (literally: liver) of the earth.'
'[Drop tranquility into the midst of the field]s. Hasten…' ʾarbdd 'tranquility, calm' (etymology debated); the pacification-formula repeats.
'[urge, speed to me your fe]et, let them race.' The race-to-me summons resumes.
'[Let them hasten to me your leg]s, to the midst of the mountain.'
'…in your hand the message-tablet.' bdk = 'in your hand'; spr = 'scribal-document / message-tablet.'
'…[in] your right hand.' ymn = 'right hand'; pair-line with bdk in line 24.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.1 col iii: top of column lost. Preserved text addresses Kothar-wa-Khasis (the divine craftsman), summoning him from his Egyptian/Mediterranean abode at Kaphtor (= Crete) and Memphis. This is the cycle's introduction of the artisan-deity who will later forge Baʿlu's weapons in KTU 1.2 IV.]

lines.notes: '[Kaphto]r the throne [of his seat, Memphis (Ḥikuptaḫ = Egypt) the land of his inheritance].' Kothar's abode-formula: Kaphtor = Crete; Ḥkpt = Egyptian Ḥwt-kʾ-Ptḥ 'House-of-the-ka-of-Ptaḥ' = Memphis. The double-abode marks Kothar as a Mediterranean-traveler god.

lines.translit: b ʾalp . šd . r[bt . kmn . l pʿn . kṯr]
lines.notes: 'In thousand acres, ten thousand hectares, to the feet of Kothar…' The distance-formula expressing the immensity between divine abodes; pair-formula ʾalp // rbt 'thousand // ten thousand.'

lines.translit: hbr . w ql . t[štḥwy . w kbd . hwt]
lines.notes: 'Bow and fall, p[rostrate yourselves and honor him].' The four-verb prostration-formula (here addressed to a pair of envoys, hence 2mp imperatives).

lines.translit: w . rgm l kṯ[r . w ḫss . ṯny . l hyn]
lines.notes: 'And speak to Koth[ar-wa-Khasis, repeat to Hayin]…' kṯr w ḫss 'Skillful-and-Clever' is the divine craftsman's binomial name; hyn 'Hayin' = the alternate name of Kothar (hyn d ḥrš ydm 'Hayin of the two skilled hands').

lines.translit: d ḥrš . y[dm . tḥm . ṯr . ʾil . ʾab]
lines.notes: '…of skilled ha[nds — Message of Bull ʾIlu, the father…]'. d ḥrš ydm 'the one of skilled hands' = Kothar's epithet; the message-formula introduces ʾIlu's commission.
'…word of the Benevolent, [the patriarch…]'. The standard ʾIlu-epithet hwt lṭpn ḥtk 'word of Lṭpn (the Benevolent) the patriarch.'
'O Kothar, in [...]'. yh = vocative particle.
'…set, for the booth(?)…' skt = 'sukkah / booth / shelter'; cf. Hebrew sukkâ — possibly an instruction to prepare a divine cultic shelter.
'…prepare in the mountain(?)…' ġr 'mountain'; ʿdb 'to prepare, arrange.'

lines.translit: ḥšk . ʿṣk . ʿb[ṣk . ʿmy . pʿnk . tlsmn]
lines.notes: 'Hasten, urge, sp[eed to me, let your feet race]…' The 'hasten-to-me' summons-formula recurs (cf. col ii:1, 22).
'…to me let [your] leg[s] hasten, to the midst of the mountain…' The race-to-me formula in its standard form.

lines.translit: ġr . ks . dm . rg[m . ʾiṯ . ly . w ʾargmk]
lines.notes: '…mountain of KS (Lel?). For there is a wo[rd that I have, and I will tell you].' rgm ʾiṯ ly w ʾargmk 'there is a word I have and I will tell you' = the standard pre-revelation formula throughout the Cycle (also at KTU 1.3 III 21; etc.).

lines.translit: hwt . w ʾaṯnyk [. rgm . ʿṣ . w lḫšt . ʾabn]
lines.notes: '…a word, and I will repeat it to you, [a word of tree and a whisper of stone…]'. The famous 'speech of tree and whisper of stone' formula (rgm ʿṣ wlḫšt ʾabn) — the mystery-revelation language, central to the Cycle's poetics; cf. KTU 1.3 III 22-24.

lines.translit: tʾunt . šmm . ʿm [. ʾarṣ . thmt . ʿmn . kbkbm]
lines.notes: '…the converse of heaven with [earth, of the deeps with the stars]…'. tʾunt 'converse, intercourse, communication'; the celestial-terrestrial-abyssal communication-formula — the cosmic-speech mystery. STRONG PARALLEL with Ps 19:1-4 'heavens declare the glory of God'; the Cycle's central revelation-vocabulary.

lines.translit: rgm . l tdʿ . nš[m . w l tbn . hmlt . ʾarṣ]
lines.notes: '…a word that humans do not know, [nor do the multitudes of the earth understand].' rgm l tdʿ nšm = 'the word that human-beings do not know'; the hidden-cosmic-speech motif. nšm = 'humans, mortals' (cf. Hebrew ʾănāšîm); hmlt ʾarṣ = 'multitude(s) of the earth.'
'…You and I will reveal [it]…' ʾibġy = G-yqtl of bġy 'to seek out, reveal'; the divine-revelation pact between ʾIlu and Kothar(?).

lines.translit: w yʿn . kṯr . w ḫss . [lk . lk . ʿnn . ʾilm]
lines.notes: 'And Kothar-wa-Khasis answered, [Go, go, O servants of the gods!]'. ʿnn ʾilm 'cloud-attendants of the gods' = the divine messengers' class; lk lk doubled imperative 'go!' (cf. Hebrew lēk lĕkâ Gen 12:1).

lines.translit: ʾatm . bštm . w ʾan [. šnt . kptr]
lines.notes: 'You two delay, but I [am far from Kaphtor]…' ʾatm 'you two' (2du); bštm 'you two delay' (the divine-time-perspective on messenger-travel).

lines.translit: l rḥq . ʾilm . ḥkp[t . l rḥq . ʾilnym]
lines.notes: 'Far for the gods (is) Memph[is, far for the divine ones]…'. The distance-of-the-divine-abodes formula; ʾilnym 'divine ones, deities' (poetic plural of ʾil).

lines.translit: ṯn . mṯpdm . tḥt . [ʿnt . ʾarṣ . ṯlṯ . mtḥ]
lines.notes: 'Two MṮPD-units under [the springs of the earth, three lengths of…]'. Cosmic-geography measurement; mṯpd a unit-of-length; ʿnt ʾarṣ 'springs of the earth' (the cosmic underwater).

lines.translit: ġyrm . ʾidk . l yt[n . pnm . ʿm . lṭpn]
lines.notes: '…of mountains. Then he indeed [set face toward the Benevolent (= ʾIlu)…]'. ʾidk 'then'; ytn pnm ʿm 'set face toward' = standard travel-formula.

lines.translit: ʾil d pʾid . tk ḫrš[n . ġr . ks]
lines.notes: '…ʾIlu the kind-hearted, to the midst of mountain [(GR) KS (= Lel)]…' d pʾid 'the merciful' (lit. 'of compassion') = standard ʾIlu-epithet; ḫršn ġr ks = 'Mount GR KS' = the abode of ʾIlu (variously Mount Lel).

lines.translit: ygly ḏd . ʾi[l . w ybʾu . qrš . mlk]
lines.notes: 'He reaches the abode of ʾI[lu, enters the dwelling-tent of the King]…'. ygly ḏd ʾil w ybʾu qrš mlk ʾab šnm = the standard 'arrives-at-ʾIlu' formula throughout the Cycle. ḏd 'pavilion/abode'; qrš 'tabernacle, tent-shrine'; cf. Hebrew miškān, qereš (the tabernacle planks Exod 26).

lines.translit: ʾab . šnm . l [pʿn . ʾil . yhbr . w yql]
lines.notes: '…Father of Years. At [the feet of ʾIlu he bows and falls]…'. ʾab šnm 'Father of Years' = ʾIlu's title — the eternal patriarch (cf. Daniel 7:9 ʿattîq yômîn 'Ancient of Days,' bidirectional comparative-mythology STRONG candidate).
'…he prostrates himself [and honors him]…'. The four-verb prostration-formula concludes the audience-introduction.

'Bull ʾIlu his fa[ther…]'. ṯr ʾil ʾabh 'Bull-El his father' = the El-as-patriarch epithet (cf. KTU 1.4 IV 47; 1.2 III 16; etc.). The bull-symbolism is theriomorphic, NOT the same Mesopotamian bull-of-heaven motif.

lines.translit: ḥš b[htm . tbnn . ḥš . trmmn . hklm]
lines.notes: 'Quick, [palaces will be built; quick, temples will be erected]…'. The famous palace-building-formula (also at KTU 1.4 V; 1.4 VI; etc.). bhtm 'palaces / great-houses'; hklm 'temples / great-halls' (loanword from Akkadian *ekallu*; cf. Hebrew hêkāl).
'In the midst of [...]'. Building-location specifier; lost.
'Among / between [...]'. bn = 'son(s)' or 'between'; lost.
'A…'. Lost.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.1 col iv: top of column lost. The preserved text is the most substantive section of KTU 1.1 — the divine banquet at which ʾIlu proclaims Yammu's elevation, gives him the new name 'Yaw' (a striking parallel to Yahweh in the Hebrew Bible — Smith 1994 vol 1, pp. 151-160), and orders Baʿlu's expulsion from kingship. This is the political setup for the duel in KTU 1.2.]

lines.notes: Severely damaged opening — multiple readings possible per Smith 1994 vol 1; first preserved cluster appears to be a divine-name or epithet.
'Aloud he cried to Q[...]'. The standard gm ṣḥ 'aloud he called' speech-formula opens a divine command.
'To the distant ones, to P[...]'. l rḥqm 'to the far ones' — addressing distant divine attendants.

'ʾIlu cried, He sits at the m[arzeaḥ-feast]…'. mrzḥ = the famous mrzeaḥ ritual-banquet (cf. Amos 6:7 marzēaḥ; Jer 16:5 bêt marzēaḥ) — the divine drinking-rite at which ʾIlu presides. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: marzeaḥ in the Hebrew Bible.
'In confusion(?), youths(?)…' bṯt unclear (possibly bṯt 'shame' or btt 'wine-skin' or 'song-line'); ʿllmn 'youths / lads / young attendants.'
'O gods, the house of your lord [...].' bt bʿlk 'the house of your lord' = the divine palace; bʿlk 'your lord' here addresses the assembly (likely Baʿlu's circumstance being arraigned).

lines.translit: d l . ylkn . ḥš . b ʾa[rṣ ...]
lines.notes: '…who does not walk quickly in the [earth/land]…'. d l ylkn 'who does not go'; ḥš 'quickly, with haste'; b ʾarṣ 'in the land' — a description of a deity who has not yet asserted dominion.
'In the dust (with) the lot(?) of the ṬTM …'. ʿpr 'dust'; ḫbl 'cord / lot / region'; ṭtm uncertain.

lines.translit: šqy . rṯan . tnmy . ytn [. ks . b yd]
lines.notes: 'Pour for me, RṮN; for me, TNMY pour. [A cup he placed in (his) hand]…'. Drinking-attendants are named (rṯn, tnmy are not divine names but cup-bearer-titles); the cup-handling formula ks b yd 'cup in hand' recurs throughout the Cycle's banquet-scenes.

'A krpn-vessel in both (literally: two) hands…'. krpn = a large drinking-vessel (cognate to Akkadian karpānu); klʾat yd 'two hands' = the dual-handed cup-holding gesture characteristic of divine drinking-scenes.

'Like words(?), like an arrow(?), they were gathered…' mll possibly 'utterance' or 'pulverization'; ḥṣ 'arrow'; tʾuspn = Gt-pf 3mp of ʾsp 'to gather, harvest.' Sense uncertain; perhaps a metaphor for the speed of the gathering deities.
'ʾIlu guards his sons, Bull [...]'. tgr 'guards, protects'; ʾil bnh 'his sons' = the divine assembly as ʾIlu's family. The father-king-of-the-pantheon framing.

lines.translit: w yʿn . lṭpn . ʾil . d p[ʾid ...]
lines.notes: 'And the Benevolent ʾIlu, the kind-hearted, answered…' lṭpn ʾil d pʾid = the full ʾIlu epithet-formula 'Benevolent ʾIlu the merciful.'

**THE NAME-GIVING SCENE — MANDATORY MAJOR**: 'The name of my son is YW, O goddess[ʾIlatu / ʾAṯiratu]…'. THIS IS THE FAMOUS YW LINE — ʾIlu names his son with the divine name YW. Smith 1994 vol 1 pp. 151-160 reads this as the etymological core of YHWH; the consonants Y-W are the same as the short Yahwistic theophoric ending (-yw, -yāhû). Bidirectional STRONG CROSS-CORPUS candidate with Yahweh-in-Israelite-religion. Note: YW here is given to YAMMU (the SEA-god), not to Baʿlu — a fact of comparative-religious significance that requires careful framing.

'And he proclaimed the name of Yammu [...]'. pʿr 'to proclaim, declare publicly' (cf. Hebrew pʿr/peh-ʿar 'open mouth wide'); šm ym 'name of Yammu (the Sea)' — the divine-name-proclamation. The previous line names him YW; this line gives him the title YM 'Sea.'
'They(/she) answered to him: We have not nourished(?)…'. tʿnyn = G-yqtl 3fp (or D-perf) of ʿny 'to answer'; zntn = uncertain (possibly zwn 'to feed/nourish' — denying his entitlement to nurture?).
'You are the lord(?), proclaim…' ʾat 'you' (2ms); ʾadn 'lord' (cf. Hebrew ʾādōn); tpʿr = 'you shall proclaim' (D-yqtl).
'I (am) the Benevolent ʾIlu, the kind-hearted…'. ʾIlu's self-identification as the proclaimer.
'Upon (my) hands I have proclaimed…'. ʿl ydm 'upon (the/my) hands' — the lifted-hand proclamation-gesture (cf. the raised-hand-of-divine-decree convention).
'Your name is Beloved of ʾI[lu]…'. mdd ʾil 'Beloved of ʾIlu' = standard epithet of Yammu (cf. KTU 1.3 III 38-39; 1.4 II 34; 1.4 VI 12 — the formula mdd ʾil ym 'Yammu Beloved of ʾIlu').
'House of my silver, which [...]'. bt kspy 'my silver house' = the silver palace, possibly the gift Yammu is to receive.
'…from the hand of Mighty Baʿ[lu]…'. bd = 'from the hand of' (b + yd); ʾaliyn bʿl = 'Mightiest Baʿlu' (one of his standard epithets).
'…when he reviles me…' kd 'when, because'; ynʾaṣn = G-yqtl 3ms + 1cs suffix of nʾṣ 'to spurn, treat with contempt.'

lines.translit: gršnn . l k[sʾi . mlkh . l nḫt . l kḥṯ]
lines.notes: 'Drive him out from [the throne of his kingship, from the dais of] (his rule)…'. gršnn 'drive him out!' (D-impv + 3ms suffix); l ksʾi mlkh 'from the throne of his kingship' = the standard kingship-deposition formula (also at KTU 1.6 V 5-6; cf. Isa 14:13 'I will sit on the mount of assembly').
'…of his dominion…'. drkt 'dominion, sovereignty' (cf. Hebrew derek 'way, dominion'); the kingship-deposition continues.
'And if also [...]'. w hm 'and if'; ap 'also, even'; l = preposition or negative.
'…he will strike you like [...]'. ymḫṣ = G-yqtl of mḫṣ 'to smite, strike' (cf. Hebrew māḥaṣ 'to crush'). The verb mḫṣ is central to the duel-vocabulary in KTU 1.2 IV.
'ʾIlu (held) a sacrifice/feast…'. dbḥ 'sacrifice, ritual-feast' (cf. Hebrew zebaḥ); ʾIlu inaugurates the divine banquet.
'He proclaimed in/at the house of [...]'. The proclamation-formula recurs.

'He slaughtered o[xen, also sheep he laid low]…'. The standard banquet-preparation formula (ṭbḫ ʾalpm ʾap ṣʾin) characteristic of divine feasts throughout the Cycle (cf. KTU 1.4 VI; 1.114 — Mesopotamian and Greek hecatomb parallels).

lines.translit: ṯrm . w [mri . ʾilm . ʿglm . dt . šnt]
lines.notes: '…bulls and [fatlings, rams, year-old calves]…'. The standard sacrificial-list-formula: ṯrm 'bulls'; mri 'fattened/choice animals'; ʿglm 'calves'; dt šnt 'of (the) year' (year-old).
'…lambs, [an abundance of kids]…'. ʾimr 'lamb' (cf. Hebrew ʾimmar in Ezra 6:9, 17; Aramaic); qmṣ 'amount, handful, abundance'; llʾim 'young rams/kids' (cf. Hebrew lîlîth and related root).

i18n.en: [KTU 1.1 col v: top destroyed. Preserved text contains fragmentary day-counting formulae and references to Mount Ṣapunu (Baʿlu's mountain), suggesting a transitional or travel scene. Smith 1994 vol 1 pp. 169-170 reads this as part of Baʿlu's escape or relocation following ʾIlu's deposition-decree.]

lines.notes: Single preserved sign.
'…[and a day, two day]s…' Standard day-counting-formula ym ymm 'day(s), days.'
'[they pass; (X) arrives at] the throat / appetite…'. yʿtqn 'they pass on'; ymġy 'arrives'; npš here likely 'throat, appetite' (the food-hunger meaning, not the soul-meaning).

'…[Had]du(?) she/they meets him…'. Hd = Haddu, the alternate name of Baʿlu (the storm-deity proper; Baʿlu 'Lord' is the cult-title; Hd is the personal name); tngṯnh = G-yqtl 3fs/3mp + 3ms suffix of ngṯ 'to meet, encounter.'

'…in Ṣapunu.' ṣpn = Mount Ṣapunu (modern Jebel al-Aqra in Syria), Baʿlu's holy mountain — the cosmic mountain analogous to Sinai/Zion. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: cf. Hebrew ṣāpôn 'north' as direction-from-Mount-Ṣapunu; Ps 48:2 yarketê ṣāpôn 'recesses of the north' applied to Mount Zion.
'…(he/they) drew(?) BʿN(?)…'. nšb possibly 'to drag, pull'; bʿn uncertain.
'…then he answered…'. bkm = 'then, after this' (compound particle); yʿn = G-yqtl of ʿny 'to answer.'
'…[I know that I do not] know…' or '[that you have known, I have] not known.' ydʿ // ydʿt parallelism on yd ʿ 'to know.'
'…they bind / you bind…'. ʾsr 'to bind' — possibly the binding-of-Yammu motif or Baʿlu's earlier defeat.
'[Bull ʾIlu …] he binds…'. ṯr ʾil 'Bull ʾIlu' epithet; rks 'to bind, tie.'
'…stones, they were polished/embraced(?)…'. ʾabn 'stone'; ʾupqt possibly 'embraces' or 'channels' (passive).
'…with the mountain of my loins / haunches.' ġr 'mountain'; mtnym 'two loins / haunches' (cf. Hebrew motnayim) — body-of-the-cosmos imagery.
'[You(?) zd…] thinness(?) of the back(?).' rq 'thin, lean'; gb 'back, hill.'
'…all of(?) guards / opens(?) his loin.' tġr 'opens / guards (a gate)'; mtn 'loin.'
'…and a day, two days…' The day-counting-formula recurs.
'[they pass …] (X) arrives at the throat.' Parallel to v.3.
'…(X) Haddu, she encounters him.' Parallel to v.4.
'…your wrath(?) in Ṣapunu.' ḥm here possibly ḥmt 'wrath' or ḥmm 'heat'; b ṣpn 'in Ṣapunu' (Baʿlu's mountain).
'…I will make to lie down a hind/doe.' ʾišqb = Š-yqtl 1cs of škb 'to lie down' (causative 'cause to lie down'); ʾaylt 'doe, hind' (cf. Hebrew ʾayyālāh) — cultic/sacrificial imagery.

'…from the spring(s) he answers.' mbkm 'springs, sources (of the deep)' (cf. Hebrew nibkê 'sources' Job 38:16, the deep-springs of the abyss); yʿn 'he answers.' STRONG CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: the deep-springs of cosmic origin.
'…I know, I do not know.' Parallel to v.8.
'…they bind, Bull ʾIlu…'. Parallel to v.9-10.
'…he binds among the stones.' rks 'binds, ties up'; bn ʾabnm 'between the stones' (locative).
'…they were polished/joined, evening(?).' ʿrb 'evening, sunset' or 'mixing.'
'[…and] the mountain of my loins — you(?) ZD(?)…'. Parallel to v.12.
'…(she/they) enters at the lifting(?).' tʿrb = G-yqtl 3fs of ʿrb 'to enter'; b šʾi 'at/by lifting' (the šʾi 'lifting' = sunrise? or 'taking-of-portion' as in a banquet?).

'…you shall not act-arrogantly, you shall not …' tzd = G-yqtl 2ms of zwd 'to act presumptuously, contend' (cf. Hebrew zîd, the root of 'arrogance,' Ps 19:14); tptq = uncertain (possibly 'tear apart' or 'release').
'…(broken) to the earth.' Final partially-preserved line of the column.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.1 col vi: destroyed — no preserved text. The end of tablet 1.1; transition to KTU 1.2 follows.]

[KTU 1.2 col i: opening lines fragmentary. The scene that unfolds: Yammu (the Sea-god) dispatches his two messengers (mlʾakm) to the divine assembly (pḫr mʿd) at Mount Lel, demanding the surrender of Baʿlu. ʾIlu and the gods abjectly submit; Baʿlu rages and must be restrained by ʿAnatu and ʿAṯtartu.]

lines.notes: Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
Opening lines lost.
'…messenger of Yammu…' mlʾak = 'messenger, envoy' (cf. Hebrew malʾāk, Greek angelos); cognate of biblical 'angel.' Yammu's diplomatic embassy is announced.

'…embassy of Judge River…'. tʿdt 'embassy, delegation' (cf. Hebrew tĕʿūdâ 'testimony'); ṯpṭ nhr 'Judge River' is Yammu's standard binomial title (ym // nhr 'Sea // River' parallelism); ṯpṭ 'judge, ruler' (cf. Hebrew šôpēṭ, šepheṭ). The Yam-Nahar pair-naming is consistent throughout the Cycle.
'[They went a thousand-(times), going(?) and ten thousand-(times) like rain(?)]'. The travel-distance formula (ʾalpm // rbt 'thousand // ten thousand' pair).

lines.translit: [ʾatr . ṯn . ṯn . hlk . ʾatr . ṯlṯ . klhm]
lines.notes: '[After two, two go; after three, all of them]'. The 'after two, after three' staircase-parallelism characteristic of Ugaritic narrative-numerology.
'[Yammu sent messengers; Judge River dispatched (envoys)]'. The verb lʾak 'to send (a messenger)' is the cognate of Hebrew lʾk (the unattested verbal root behind malʾāk 'messenger').
'[Message of Yammu, your lord; your master, Judge…]'. tḥm 'message of (X)' — the standard message-delivery formula (cf. Adapa B; throughout ANE epistolography).

lines.translit: [nhr . tn . ʾilm . d tqh . d tqyn . hmlt]
lines.notes: '[River — Give up, O gods, the one whom you fear, the one whom multitudes revere]'. tn = 'give!' (impv); ʾilm 'gods' (vocative); d tqh 'whom you fear' (relative + G-yqtl 2mp of yrʾ 'to fear'); hmlt 'multitudes.'

lines.translit: [tn . bʿl . w ʿnnh . bn . dgn . ʾarṯm . pḏh]
lines.notes: **MANDATORY**: 'Give up Baʿlu and his attendants, the Son of Dagan, that I may take his gold!'. bn dgn 'Son of Dagan' = Baʿlu's parentage (Dagan/Dagon = the West-Semitic grain-deity; cf. Judges 16; 1 Sam 5). pḏh 'his gold/wealth' (cf. Hebrew pdh 'to redeem' — the redemption-payment metaphor). Yammu demands Baʿlu's submission with confiscation-of-property.
'[The lads/youths set out, they did not turn back; then face]…'. ġlm 'young man, attendant'; tbʿ = G-pf 3mp of nbʿ 'to set forth'; ʾidk 'thereupon.'

lines.translit: [l ytn . tk . ġr . ll . ʿm . pḫr . mʿd]
lines.notes: '[were set toward Mount Lel, toward the assembled assembly]'. ġr ll 'Mount Lel' = ʾIlu's abode; pḫr mʿd 'gathered assembly' — the divine council. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: the bĕnê hāʾĕlōhîm convening before YHWH (Job 1:6; 2:1; Ps 82:1; 89:6-8); cf. Akkadian *puḫru ša ilāni*.

lines.translit: [ʾap . ʾilm . l lḥm . yṯb . bn . qdš]
lines.notes: '[Indeed the gods were sitting down to eat, the holy sons]…'. lḥm 'to eat / bread'; bn qdš 'sons of the holy one' = the divine council (cf. bĕnê hāqqōdeš).

lines.translit: [l . trm . bʿl . qm . ʿl . ʾil . hlm . ʾilm]
lines.notes: '[to feast; Baʿlu stood beside ʾIlu. Lo, the gods]…'. trm 'to feast, dine'; qm ʿl 'stood beside / over'; hlm 'lo, behold.'
'[saw them; they saw the messengers of Yammu, the embassy of Judge…]'. tphhm 'they saw them'; tphn = parallel verb (alternate stem). The arrival-perceived formula.

lines.translit: [nhr . tġly . ʾilm . rʾiš[t]hm . l ẓr . brkthm]
lines.notes: '[River. The gods lowered their heads to the top of their knees]'. tġly = D-yqtl 3fp of ġly 'to lower'; rʾišthm 'their heads'; ẓr 'top, summit'; brkthm 'their knees.' THE FAMOUS HEADS-TO-KNEES gesture of divine fear — the gods bow in fear before Yammu's envoys. Cross-corpus the Hebrew 'putting head between knees' (1 Kings 18:42 Elijah at Carmel; possibly a posture of supplication/lamentation).

lines.translit: [w l . kḥṯ . zblhm . bhm . yg]ʿr . bʿl
lines.notes: '[and to the thrones of their princely-seats. Baʿlu re]bukes them.' kḥṯ 'throne, dais' (cf. Hebrew kissēʾ); zblhm 'their princely-rule' (cf. Hebrew zĕbûl 'lofty habitation,' the name Zebulun); ygʿr 'he rebukes' (cf. Hebrew gāʿar — God's rebuke of the sea Ps 18:15, 104:7; Isa 17:13).
'Why have you lowered, O gods, your heads…'. lm 'why?' (cf. Hebrew lāmâ); ġltm = G-pf 2mp of ġly 'to lower'; rʾištkm 'your heads.' Baʿlu shames the assembled gods for their cowardly posture.

lines.translit: l ẓr . brktkm . w l . kḥṯ . zblkm
lines.notes: '…to the top of your knees, and to the thrones of your princely-rule?'. Repetition of v.24 in Baʿlu's reproach.

lines.translit: ʾaḥd . ʾilm . tʿny . lḥt . mlʾak . ym
lines.notes: 'Let one of the gods answer the tablets of the messengers of Yammu…'. ʾaḥd 'one'; tʿny 'let (him) answer'; lḥt 'tablets, messages' (cf. Hebrew lûaḥ 'tablet').

lines.translit: tʿdt . ṯpṭ . nhr . tšʾu . ʾilm . rʾišthm
lines.notes: '…the embassy of Judge River. The gods raised their heads…'. tšʾu = G-yqtl 3fp of nšʾ 'to lift, raise.' The gods straighten themselves in response to Baʿlu's reproach.

lines.translit: l ẓr . brkthm . w l . kḥṯ . zblhm
lines.notes: '…from the top of their knees, and from the thrones of their princely-rule.' Posture-reversal.

lines.translit: ʾaḫr . tmġyn . mlʾak . ym . tʿdt . ṯpṭ . nhr
lines.notes: 'Afterward, the messengers of Yammu arrive, the embassy of Judge River.'. ʾaḫr 'afterward'; tmġyn = G-yqtl 3mp/dual of mġy 'to arrive.'

lines.translit: l pʿn . ʾil . [l] tpl . l tštḥwy . pḫr . mʿd
lines.notes: 'At the feet of ʾIlu they do [not] fall, they do not bow down (to) the assembled assembly.' THE FAMOUS NON-PROSTRATION: Yammu's envoys refuse the required obeisance, a diplomatic affront. l tpl 'they fall not'; l tštḥwy 'they bow not.'

'Standing they spoke their word, standing they spoke (their word).' qmm 'standing' (dual participle); ʾaṯrm uncertain (perhaps 'striding' or 'in position'); ʾamr 'they spoke / their word.' The standing-while-speaking posture compounds the diplomatic insult.

lines.translit: ʾišt . ʾištm . yʾitmr . ḥrb . lṭšt [b lšnhm]
lines.notes: 'Fire, two fires they kindle, a sharpened sword [is on their tongues].' ʾišt 'fire'; yʾitmr possibly G-yqtl with metathesis of ʾmr or 'to flame'; ḥrb lṭšt 'a sharpened sword'; b lšnhm 'on their tongues' (cf. Hebrew Ps 57:5 ḥarbôt ulšônām 'their tongues like sharp swords'; Ps 64:4; Prov 12:18; James 3:6). STRONG CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: the sword-tongue, hostile-speech-as-weapon trope.

lines.translit: rgm . l ṯr . ʾabh . ʾil . tḥm . ym . bʿlkm
lines.notes: 'They spoke to Bull, his father, ʾIlu: Message of Yammu, your lord…'. rgm 'they spoke'; ṯr ʾabh ʾil 'Bull his father ʾIlu' = the standard El-as-father epithet (Smith 1994 vol 1 reads ʾabh as 'his father,' a standard El-paternity formula).

lines.translit: ʾadnkm . ṯpṭ . nhr . tn . ʾilm . d tqh
lines.notes: '…your master, Judge River. Give up, O gods, the one whom you fear…'. The demand-formula resumes (parallel to v.17).

lines.translit: d tqyn . hmlt . tn . bʿl . w ʿnnh
lines.notes: '…whom multitudes revere — Give up Baʿlu and his attendants…'. Parallel to v.18.

lines.translit: bn . dgn . ʾarṯm . pḏh . w yʿn . ṯr . ʾabh . ʾil
lines.notes: '…the Son of Dagan, that I may take his gold. And Bull, his father, ʾIlu answered…'. The Father-El answers the demand.

lines.translit: ʿbdk . bʿl . y ymm . ʿbdk . bʿl
lines.notes: **THE FATEFUL CONCESSION**: 'Your servant is Baʿlu, O Yammu! Your servant is Baʿlu…'. ʿbdk 'your servant' = the formal subjection-formula. ʾIlu submissively hands Baʿlu over to Yammu. This is the central political-crisis of the Cycle.

'…[Ri]vers; the Son of Dagan — your prisoner he (will be), he will bring (tribute)…'. ʾasrkm 'your prisoner / one bound to you'; ybl 'he will bring / pay tribute' (cf. Hebrew yābal 'to bring as tribute').

'…I will give you tribute as the gods [pay]…'. ʾargmnk 'your tribute' (cf. Hebrew ʾargāmān 'purple/tribute' — Persian *arghavān? possibly Akkadian argamannu); the tribute-language is cognate to the purple-dye/tribute Akkadian financial-vocabulary.
'…like sons of the holy one, gifts(?) for you…'. tšy possibly 'gift, tribute' (denominal from a verb meaning 'present, offer').
'…even/also, the Prince Baʿlu was furious…'. ʾanš 'angry, furious'; zbl bʿl 'Prince Baʿlu' (zbl = 'prince, exalted one'). Baʿlu's rage erupts.

'[He took in (his) hand] a striking-(weapon), in (his) right hand a mʿsṣt …'. ʾiḫd 'he took, grasped'; ʾaṣṭ uncertain (possibly a weapon); the line shows Baʿlu reaching for arms — restrained in the next line.

lines.translit: ymnh . ʿnt . tʾuḫd . ymnh . ʿṯtrt . tʾuḫd [šmʾalh]
lines.notes: **MANDATORY**: 'His right hand ʿAnatu seized; (his) right hand ʿAṯtartu seized [his left hand]'. ʿAnatu and ʿAṯtartu (the two warrior-goddesses, cousins-or-sister-pair) restrain Baʿlu from striking the envoys. NOTE: ʿṯtrt = ʿAṯtartu (the Northwest-Semitic ancestress of Hebrew ʿaštōret, Greek Astarte, Aramaic ʿtrt-Atargatis). The two-goddess restraint scene.

lines.translit: ʾik . mġnt . [mlʾak] ym . tʿdt . ṯpṭ . nhr
lines.notes: 'How can you strike the messengers of Yammu, the embassy of Judge River?' ʾik 'how?' (interrogative); mġnt = D-yqtl 2ms of mġn 'to strike, smite'(?) — though some readings parse this as mġnt 'gift, present' (cf. Hebrew māgēn 'shield'). The goddesses restrain Baʿlu by appealing to messenger-immunity.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.2 col ii: broken away entirely. The lost text is reconstructed from context (Smith 1994 vol 1 pp. 290-294): the central scene likely contained (i) Baʿlu's complaint or vow following the messengers' departure; (ii) the conference with Kothar-wa-Khasis (the divine craftsman); (iii) possibly the initial forging-instruction for the magical weapons Yagrush and Ayamur that will appear in column iv.]

[KTU 1.2 col iii: top of column lost. Preserved text contains a dialogue scene — possibly Kothar-wa-Khasis blessing Baʿlu's enterprise and predicting the defeat of his enemies; possibly also ʾAṯtart/ʿAnat petitioning ʾIlu on Baʿlu's behalf. Lineation per Smith 1994 vol 1.]

lines.notes: Top of column destroyed.
Top of column destroyed.
Top of column destroyed.
'[And] Kothar-wa-Khasis [answered]…'. The divine craftsman opens his speech-act.
'[To declare] to Mighty Baʿlu…'. lrgm = preposition l + infinitive 'to speak'; ʾaliyn bʿl 'Mightiest Baʿlu' epithet.
'O ʾIwrkl(?), live(?)…'. ʾiwrkl an obscure divine epithet (possibly a hypocoristic name); ḥwy 'live, may you live' (cf. Hebrew ḥāyê).
'…(may) Ḥarranu burn your he[ad]…'. tbʿrn 'they/she will burn'; ḥrn = either the deity Ḥōrōn (a curse-divinity) or 'noble curse'; rʾiš 'head.' A curse-formula directed at Baʿlu's enemies.
'…ʿAṯtartu, name of Baʿlu, (smash) your crown!…'. qdqd 'crown of the head, scalp' (cf. Hebrew qodqōd). This is the famous Yam-shall-be-smitten-on-the-head curse — anticipating the duel resolution.
'…(may) she strike your crown…'. tmḫṣ = G-yqtl 3fs of mḫṣ 'to smite'; qdqdk 'your crown.' Anticipating the duel's outcome — the head-smiting motif.
'…you shall pour out(?) your sigh, [Prince Yammu]…'. tʿrk uncertain; ʾanyk 'your groaning'; zbl ym 'Prince Yammu' (Yammu's standard epithet, paralleling zbl bʿl).
'…you shall pour out your sigh, Judge [River]…'. Parallel — ṯpṭ nhr 'Judge River' (the binomial).
'…he took one [...]'. yqḥ 'he took' (cf. Hebrew lāqaḥ); ʾaḫd 'one.'
'[And] the Benevolent ʾIlu [the kind-hearted answered]…'. The standard ʾIlu-introduction formula.
'…servant am I, an attendant…'. ʿbd ʾan 'I am a servant'; ʿnn 'attendant, cloud-rider.' Possibly Baʿlu's complaint about being made Yammu's servant.

'[ʾAṯiratu and her sons], ʾIlatu [and the household of her kindred]…'. ʾaṯrt 'ʾAṯiratu' = Asherah; bnh 'her sons' (the bnei ʾilm 'sons of the gods'); ʾilt 'the goddess' (= ʾAṯiratu's title); ṣbrt ʾaryh 'gathering of her kin.' STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: ʾAṯiratu is the Northwest-Semitic ancestress of biblical Asherah.
'[How] can you smite Mighty Baʿlu…?'. tmḫṣ 'you smite' (2ms); the head-of-pantheon questioning the proposed deposition.
'[How] can you answer [Prince] Baʿlu [of the earth]?'. zbl bʿl ʾarṣ 'Prince Baʿlu of the Earth' = Baʿlu's third standard epithet (zbl bʿl ʾarṣ; also at KTU 1.5 VI 10; 1.6 III 9, 21; etc.).
'…the going of Baʿlu…'. hlk 'going, walking, march.'
'…go, O Yammu, your lord…'. The hostile-mocking speech direction.
'[Furious was Prince] Baʿlu…'. ʾanš zbl bʿl = 'the Prince Baʿlu was angry' — the rage-of-Baʿlu refrain.
Lost.
Lost.
Lost.
'…Kothar…'. kṯr 'Kothar' — the craftsman-deity reappears.
'…I shall call/proclaim…'. ʾiqraʾ = G-yqtl 1cs of qrʾ 'to call' (cf. Hebrew qārāʾ). Closing line of the preserved column.

i18n.en: [KTU 1.2 col iv: top fragmentary; lower text is the most famous scene in the entire Cycle — the DUEL OF BAʿLU AND YAMMU. Kothar-wa-Khasis forges two magical mace-weapons named Yagrush (yet to drive') and Ayamur ('Driver'); Baʿlu strikes Yammu twice; Yammu collapses; Baʿlu's kingship is proclaimed by ʿAṯtartu and the gods.]

lines.notes: Top of column fragmentary.
Top of column fragmentary.
'…horn(?)…'. qrn 'horn' — possibly part of an epithet of Yammu-as-horned-bull or a feature of the weapon.
'[And] Kothar-wa-Khasis answered…'. The divine craftsman addresses Baʿlu before the duel.

lines.translit: l rgmt . lk . l zbl . bʿl
lines.notes: 'Did I not declare to you, O Prince Baʿlu…?'. l rgmt 'did I not speak' (interrogative l + perfect); the I-told-you-so rhetorical opening.

'…(did I not) repeat to you, O Rider on the Clouds?'. ṯnt 'I repeated'; rkb ʿrpt 'Rider on the Clouds' = THE central epithet of Baʿlu (also KTU 1.2 IV 8, 29; 1.3 II 40; 1.3 IV 4; 1.4 III 11, V 7, etc.). MANDATORY MAJOR CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: rōkēb bāʿărābôt 'Rider on the Clouds' (Ps 68:5); the New Testament Christological appropriation (Matt 26:64; Rev 1:7); the Son of Man on clouds (Dan 7:13). Strong central candidate.

lines.translit: ht . ʾibk . bʿlm . ht . ʾibk . tmḫṣ
lines.notes: 'Now your enemy, O Baʿlu, now your enemy you shall strike…'. ht 'now'; ʾibk 'your enemy' (cf. Hebrew ʾōyēb); the imminent-victory declaration.

lines.translit: ht . tṣmt . ṣrtk . tqḥ . mlk . ʿlmk
lines.notes: '…now you shall annihilate your foe. You shall take your eternal kingship…'. tṣmt 'you destroy, annihilate'; ṣrt 'foe, oppressor'; mlk ʿlmk 'your eternal kingship' (mlk ʿlm = 'everlasting kingship,' cognate to Hebrew malkût ʿōlām, Ps 145:13).
'…your dominion of generation-upon-generation.' drkt 'dominion'; dt drdr 'of generation-upon-generation' (cf. Hebrew dōr wādôr, lədōr wādōr — Ps 89:2 — STRONG PARALLEL).

'Kothar fashioned two maces (lit: bindings)…'. ṣmdm 'two maces / clubs / fastenings' (dual); yṣmd = G-yqtl of ṣmd 'to bind, fashion (a mace).' THE FORGING OF THE TWO WEAPONS — the central object of the duel narrative.
'…and he pro[claimed their (two) names]…'. ypʿr 'he proclaims, declares with the mouth'; šmthm 'their two names.' The name-giving ritual that activates the weapons.

**THE FIRST WEAPON'S NAME**: 'Your name, you (= the first mace), is Yagrush!'. ygrš = 'May-he-drive-out' (G-yqtl 3ms of grš 'to drive out, expel'; cf. Hebrew gāraš, the verb of expulsion-from-Eden Gen 3:24). The mace IS its function: a speech-act-activated weapon. STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cognate to Hebrew gāraš in the Genesis 3:24 expulsion-from-Eden motif.
**THE PERFORMATIVE NAMING**: 'Yagrush — drive out Yam!'. The pun and command: the name commands its function. grš ym 'drive out Yammu!' (D-impv of grš).
'Drive out Yammu from his throne…'. l ksʾih 'from his throne' — the deposition-from-throne language; STRONG CROSS-CORPUS: cf. Isa 14:13, the deposition-of-Shahar-ben-Helal; Ps 89:5.
'…Nahar from the throne-dais of his dominion!'. nhr 'River' (Yammu's binomial); kḥṯ drkt 'dais of dominion' = standard kingship-vocabulary; the deposition continues.
'You shall leap from the hand of Baʿlu…'. trtqṣ = Gt-yqtl 2fs of rqṣ 'to dance, leap'; b yd bʿl 'from the hand of Baʿlu.' The mace is commanded to fly from Baʿlu's hand at the target.
'…like an eagle from his fingers!'. nšr 'eagle, vulture' (cf. Hebrew nešer); ʾuṣbʿt 'fingers' (cf. Hebrew ʾeṣbaʿ). The eagle-flight simile for the weapon's trajectory.
'Strike the shoulder of Prince Yammu…'. hlm 'strike!' (G-impv of hlm); ktp 'shoulder' (cf. Hebrew kātēp); zbl ym 'Prince Yammu' (the standard epithet).
'…between the hands(?) (= chest/shoulders) of Judge River!'. bn ydm 'between the hands / on the chest'; ṯpṭ nhr 'Judge River' (the binomial completion).
'The mace leapt from the hand of Baʿlu…'. yrtqṣ = Gt-pf 3ms (the mace LEAPS, performing what was commanded); the weapon obeys.
'…like an eagle from his fingers.' Repetition of v.17 in the narrative-perfect.
'It struck the shoulder of Prince Yammu…'. ylm = Gt-pf 3ms (or G-pres 'it strikes'); the weapon hits its target.
'…between the hands of Judge River.' The blow lands.

'But Yammu was strong, he did not collapse…'. ʿz 'strong, mighty' (cf. Hebrew ʿōz); l ymk 'he did not sink/fall' (G-yqtl 3ms negative; cf. Hebrew māk 'to be low, sink'). YAMMU DOES NOT FALL TO THE FIRST BLOW — the duel intensifies.

lines.translit: l tnġṣn . pnth . l ydlp . tmnh
lines.notes: '…his joints did not collapse, his frame did not crumble.' tnġṣn 'they shake/break' (G-yqtl 3fp negative); pnth 'his joints' (cf. Hebrew pinnâ 'corner, structural-element'); ydlp 'it drips/crumbles' (cf. Hebrew dālap, leaking-roof); tmn 'frame, build.' Yammu remains standing.
'Kothar binds(?) two (more) maces…'. yṯʿr possibly 'arranges, prepares' (D-yqtl); or 'announces (a second naming).' The second weapon enters the scene.
'…and he proclaims their (two) names.' The second naming-ritual.

**THE SECOND WEAPON'S NAME**: 'Your name, you (= the second mace), is Ayamur!'. ʾaymr = 'Driver' (etymology from mwr or ʾamr 'to drive away, expel'). Some readings translate as 'Cast-Out' or 'Expeller.' The second weapon, like the first, IS its function.
**THE PERFORMATIVE NAMING (2nd)**: 'Ayamur — drive away Yammu!'. mr 'drive away! / cast out!' (G-impv); the speech-act activates the weapon's function.
'Drive Yammu from his throne…'. Parallel structure to v.14: the deposition-language is repeated for the second weapon.
'…Nahar from the throne-dais of his dominion!'. Parallel to v.15.
'You shall leap from the hand of Baʿlu…'. Parallel to v.16.
'…like an eagle from his fingers!'. Parallel to v.17.

**THE SECOND BLOW**: 'Strike the CROWN of Prince Yammu…'. qdqd 'crown of the head, scalp' (the same word foreshadowed in 1.2 III 8-9). MANDATORY CROSS-CORPUS PARALLEL: Hebrew māḥaṣ qodqōd ('smite the head') in Ps 68:22 'God will smite the head (qodqōd) of his enemies'; Hab 3:13; Deut 33:20. The head-smiting motif of cosmic-victory.
'…between the eyes of Judge River!'. bn ʿnm 'between the eyes' (cf. Hebrew bên ʿênayim — the forehead). The target shifts UP from the chest (1st blow) to the head (2nd blow) — escalation.

**THE FALL**: 'Yammu collapsed, he fell to the earth…'. yprsḥ 'he collapses, sinks down' (Gt-yqtl 3ms; cf. Hebrew prs 'to spread' — in the metaphorical 'spread-himself-out-in-defeat' sense); yql 'he falls.' Yammu finally falls.
'…his joints shake, his frame crumbles.' Parallel-inversion of v.25: what did NOT happen with the first blow now happens with the second. The vocabulary of structural-defeat.

'Baʿlu drew(?) — and he drank Yam(?) / drained Yammu.' yqṯ uncertain (possibly 'gathers up, draws together' or 'destroys'); yšt = G-yqtl of šty 'to drink' (cf. Hebrew šātâ); the line is the famous crux. Smith 1994 vol 1 reads this as 'Baʿlu drags Yam' (yqṯ as 'draws to himself') — i.e., the dismemberment-victory.
'…he finishes off (= annihilates) Judge River.' ykly = D-yqtl of kly 'to bring to an end, annihilate' (cf. Hebrew kālâ, kālāl). The kill-shot.

**THE PROCLAMATION**: 'By name, ʿAṯtartu (= Astarte) rebukes (him)…'. b šm 'by name'; tgʿrm = D-yqtl 3fs + enclitic m of gʿr 'to rebuke' (cf. the same verb at 1.2 I 25, Baʿlu's rebuke of the gods; cf. Hebrew gāʿar — God's rebuke of the sea, Ps 18:15). ʿAṯtartu's voice closes the duel-scene.
